credentials.description: Notch Pay public key, sent as is in Authorization; a key containing test_ works in sandbox (same host for test and live)
Notch Pay private key, sent as is in X-Grant, for transfers, beneficiaries, balance and webhooks

example_prompt: Register a Notch Pay webhook to receive payment.complete and payment.failed events at my endpoint.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint URL that will receive webhook event payloads.

events.description: List of event types to subscribe to.

description.description: Optional human-readable label for this webhook endpoint.

id.description: Unique webhook endpoint ID. Store this to update or delete the webhook later.

gotchas: The webhook URL must be HTTPS. HTTP URLs are rejected with a 422 error.
Store the endpoint.id from the response — it is required to call update_webhook or delete_webhook later.
The events array must not be empty. Subscribing to no events is rejected. Only subscribe to event types your server actually handles.

Authorization takes your public key as is, with no 'Bearer ' prefix, and X-Grant your private key (Notch Pay's Authentication page: `-H "Authorization: YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY"` `-H "X-Grant: YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY"`).
This API registers the webhook configuration on the Notch Pay side. To validate incoming payloads, you must verify the X-Notch-Signature header on your receiving endpoint.

This endpoint also requires the `X-Grant` header carrying your private key (`X-Grant: YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY`). Without it Notch Pay returns 403 "This endpoint requires additional authentication"; a wrong value returns 403 "Invalid grant key".
